what_its_for: Phenelzine is used to treat depression, especially when other antidepressants have not worked well. It belongs to a group of medicines called MAO inhibitors (MAOIs). It can also help with anxiety and phobias.
how_to_take: Take phenelzine by mouth, exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Do not crush or chew the tablets — swallow them whole. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember. Do NOT suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause problems.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 15 mg (one tablet) taken three times a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose based on how you respond. The typical dose range is 15 mg to 90 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within a couple of hours of when you were supposed to take it. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. NEVER take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store phenelzine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused medicine safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: IMPORTANT — Phenelzine has serious food and drug interactions that can be life-threatening. AVOID these foods and drinks: aged cheeses (like cheddar, brie, blue cheese), cured or smoked meats (salami, pepperoni, sausage), pickled or fermented foods, soy sauce, tap beer and red wine, overripe or dried fruits, and broad bean pods (fava beans). AVOID these medicines: other antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics), stimulants, decongestants like pseudoephedrine or phenylephrine found in cold medicines, dextromethorphan (found in cough medicines), meperidine (Demerol), and certain migraine medicines called triptans. Avoid alcohol completely. Do not take any new prescription, over-the-counter, or herbal medicines (especially St. John's Wort) without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first. Tell ALL your healthcare providers that you are taking phenelzine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room RIGHT AWAY if you have: a sudden severe headache (the worst of your life), stiff neck, fast or pounding heartbeat, sweating, fever, chest pain, sudden vision changes, or nausea and vomiting — these could be signs of a dangerous spike in blood pressure called a hypertensive crisis. Also call your doctor if you feel more depressed, have thoughts of harming yourself or suicide, experience unusual mood changes, feel very restless or agitated, develop muscle stiffness, confusion, or a high fever (possible serotonin syndrome). Seek help immediately if any of these occur.
when_it_works: Phenelzine may take 2 to 4 weeks before you start to notice improvement in your mood. Some people may need up to 6 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it even if you do not feel better right away — be patient and keep taking it as directed. Talk to your doctor if you are not seeing any improvement after several weeks.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with extra caution — older people may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and falls. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as it may not be safe. Children and teenagers: This medicine is generally not recommended for people under 18 years old. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments may be needed. Switching antidepressants: There must be a waiting period (washout period) of at least 14 days when switching between phenelzine and most other antidepressants — your doctor will guide you through this safely.
